chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who prays in congregation in his house in Makkah, is it superior or (him praying) alone in the Sacred Masjid? So he said: 'Alone'.
ai.seo_question: Is it better to pray in congregation at home in Makkah or pray alone in the Grand Mosque?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies a specific legal nuance: while congregational prayer is generally superior, the unique sanctity of the Sacred Masjid outweighs the benefit of congregation when compared to a private home. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intrinsic merit of the location (*makān*) in Makkah, distinguishing it from general mosques where congregational prayer (*jamāʿah*) typically holds precedence. The hadith thus serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims seeking to maximize spiritual reward during their prayers in the holiest site.
